title: Cross-deployment timeout fanout from Dedicated maintenance -> Hosted API 5xxs: graceful fallback and retry dampening
creator: Alina Mercer
description: Summary: During a planned Dedicated GPU pool maintenance we observed cascading timeouts that amplified into a tenant-visible 5xx wave on the Hosted API. This ticket tracks the triage, emergency mitigation (hotfix), customer communications, and next-step engineering changes to avoid recurrence. The core issue spans maintenance drain behavior in Dedicated, edge router backpressure, and SDK retry semantics that amplified client retries.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger a controlled maintenance drain in a Dedicated pool (simulate graceful GPU shutdown).
2) Immediately route a mix of long-sequence generation requests from a heavy tenant to the same region.
3) Observe RPC timeouts from Dedicated control-plane to serving instances; requests get proxied/fanned out to fallback hosted model variants.
4) On client side, unsafely configured SDKs retry aggressively (no idempotency token) leading to request amplification.
Expected: requests should be shed or fast-failed with clear error and retry guidance. Actual: progressive host timeouts + 502/504 5xxs with high request fanout.
investigation_notes:
- Initial alert triggered by dashboard rule: hosted-api 5xx rate > 2x baseline for tenant T-ALPHA in us-west-2.
- Traces show increased latency and timeouts originating at edge-router -> dedicated-proxy hop.
- Dedicated maintenance job initiated drain but did not advertise reduced capacity to control-plane for 12s due to a bug in drain RPC (backoff loop reset).
- Edge routing policy attempted hedging to fallback model variants (model-fallback group), causing extra backend calls.
- SDK telemetry indicates many clients had retry windows of 10s with exponential backoff starting at 250ms, leading to retry storms when underlying requests entered slowpath.
- KV cache warmup on fallback models increased token compute time; combined with aggressive client retries led to connection exhaustion at gateway.
- Root cause contributors: (a) incomplete drain handshake from Dedicated -> control plane; (b) hedging policy too eager during partial capacity; (c) lack of tenant-level fast-fail and per-tenant circuit breakers at edge; (d) no centralized idempotency enforcement for generation APIs.

decisions: 1) Emergency: disable model hedging during capacity transitions (edge config override). 2) Hotfix: patch drain RPC to include explicit capacity-decrement notification (small patch applied to dedicated-proxy). 3) Longer-term: implement per-tenant circuit breaker + token TTL for retries and an edge-level retry-dampening middleware that enforces idempotency tokens for generation endpoints. 4) Add maintenance semaphore: all maintenance/drain jobs must assert 'reduced capacity' flag to control-plane before node termination proceeds.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Edge retry-dampening middleware merged and deployed to staging; rejects retries for requests without idempotency token with 429 guidance.
2) Drain handshake instrumentation in Dedicated shows <1s median advertise-time in staging and production.
3) Per-tenant circuit breaker defaults in edge-router implemented with sane defaults (open on 25% error rate sustained over 30s) and tested under simulated tenant surge.
4) Customer-facing postmortem published and affected customers have received comms.
5) SDK guidance updated and linked from the mitigation KB.

postmortem_summary:
Root cause: interplay of a delayed Dedicated drain handshake and an overly eager model fallback/hedging policy at edge combined with client-side aggressive retries.
Corrective actions taken: hotpatch to drain handshake, disabled hedging during transitions, applied per-tenant short-term reject threshold, drafted SDK guidance.
Long-term: idempotency enforcement, retry-dampening middleware, per-tenant circuit-breaker, improved maintenance protocol.
Follow-ups scheduled across SRE, Edge, SDK, and Product teams.
notes_for_oncall:
- If 5xx spike observed again, immediately: (1) enable edge emergency reject for region (config toggle); (2) disable hedging/fallback models; (3) throttle tenant causing the surge; (4) contact Dedicated on-call to verify drain status.
- Run the reproduce script in /ops/maintenance-sim to validate mitigation before re-enabling hedging.
